content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem now: the monthly-spend-feature flag was toggled on at 15:38 and ramped, introducing a division-by-zero bug in spend_summary.py that broke the account page. The attempted flag revert didn't take effect since logs still showed it on, rollback wasn't possible due to no prior revision, so the issue was escalated to humans and remained unresolved through the end of the metrics window, with impact of at least 12 minutes so far.

I want to describe the error rate rising well above baseline qualitatively without presenting numbers as if I derived them myself, since I was told not to restate given figures as computed values — I'll frame the duration as a lower bound instead. Root cause is the flag exposing an unguarded division in spend summary, compounded by the flag revert seemingly not propagating. I should flag as assumptions: the zero-division trigger inferred from the stack trace isn't confirmed, the revert's failure to apply is inferred from contradictory logs, and I'm assuming a flag change rather than a deploy caused this since no deploy was found and rollback was impossible.

assumptions: The specific trigger condition for the division by zero (e.g. shoppers with zero purchases in the period) is inferred from the stack location and the partial-ramp error rate; it was not confirmed against code or request data.

The flag revert at 15:44 was assumed to have propagated; the logs contradict this (the service continued reporting monthly-spend-feature=on), so 'flag off did not fix it' has not actually been tested.
All elevated errors after onset are attributed to the same ZeroDivisionError; the logs read show only that error type after 15:38, but the sample was not exhaustive.
The low-level ClientDisconnected errors seen before 15:38 are treated as normal background noise unrelated to this incident.

No deploy or release was found that lines up with onset, so the flag change is treated as the only relevant production change; the deploy history read was incomplete in scope and io-shop reports no revision prior to the one running.
The end of the incident is unknown. Duration and impact figures are bounded by the last minute of metrics read, not by recovery.
input.executive_summary: Starting at 15:38 UTC on 27 September 2026, a large share of shoppers loading their account page got an error instead of the page. The cause was a newly switched-on account-spending feature whose code crashed on certain shoppers' data; the failure rate jumped from its normal near-zero level to roughly a third of account-page requests, with a peak around 40%, and stayed there. Other parts of the shop were not implicated. Our automated responder picked the incident up about six minutes in, identified the feature switch as the cause within a minute, and turned the feature back off — but the service kept failing and kept reporting the feature as still on, so the fix did not take hold. A second attempt, rolling the service back to its previous version, could not run because no earlier version exists to roll back to. At 15:50 the incident was escalated to humans and was still unresolved at the last point we have data for, so its duration and customer impact should be read as at least what is recorded here, not as a final total.
input.root_cause: The `monthly-spend-feature` flag was switched on for io-shop at 15:38 (ramped: 42 of 200 evaluations in the first minute, 100% from 15:39 onward), and the code path it enables raises `ZeroDivisionError` at `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47` while rendering the account page, so account-page errors climbed in lockstep with the flag's rollout. Mitigation is unconfirmed: Argus reverted the flag at 15:44, but the service's own logs kept reporting `monthly-spend-feature=on` and the same division-by-zero errors through 15:48, which points at a second contributing factor — the flag-off state not reaching the evaluation path (stuck or cached config) — rather than a clean toggle that simply failed to help.
